Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: World Bank states government payments (salaries/pensions) are manual and there is no G2P/P2G digitalization strategy; however, it documents a humanitarian cash transfer pilot after the 2021 Bata explosion where ~300 families received support via MUNI SIMs/ATM ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). This supports limited G2P use rather than active nationwide programs.

revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank's 2023 Digital Economy Diagnostic states civil-service salaries/pensions are still paid manually with no national G2P/P2G strategy, evidenced only by an ad hoc 2021 humanitarian cash-transfer pilot (Bata explosion, ~300 families via MUNI SIMs/ATM). Local reporting (June 2025) confirms a planned payroll digitisation platform (with Moroccan firm M2M) remains at the terms-of-reference/draft-contract stage, not yet operational. Value Code 2 (Limited Use) confirmed.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: World Bank notes COBAC issued consumer protection regulation (Reg. 01-20, 2020, effective 2021) and that Equatorial Guinea has a national consumer protection/education body (CNEF) since 2019, with plans for a financial mediator ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). This indicates a consumer protection framework exists regionally and nationally, though operational maturity appears limited (e.g., complaint data not yet published).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial. The COBAC Regulation 01/20/CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC text (in force from 1 January 2021, applicable CEMAC-wide from 2023) is verified: it explicitly covers credit, microfinance and payment institutions (Art. 3) across 54 articles on fees, minimum service and unfair practices. However, World Bank (2023) confirms Equatorial Guinea has no domestic financial inclusion strategy and its national consumer body (CNEF) has not yet stood up a financial mediator, so national implementation/enforcement remains incomplete. Value Code 2 (Partial) confirmed.

Comments: DLA Piper’s Equatorial Guinea data protection summary includes a section “Breach notification” stating the law provides for a mandatory breach duty ([DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – Equatorial Guinea](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=GQ)). While details on timing/recipient are not clearly specified in the summary, it indicates mandatory requirements exist.

revision_notes: Confirmed as Mandatory. DLA Piper's dedicated 'Breach notification' page for Equatorial Guinea confirms Law 1/2016 (arts 39-40) creates a mandatory breach duty with severity-graded sanctions. A 2026 independent legal summary (Anurag Verma) corroborates that controllers must notify both the supervisory authority and affected data subjects, though the supervisory body (Órgano Rector) remains non-operational, limiting practical enforcement. Value Code 3 (Mandatory) confirmed.

Comments: BEAC’s website indicates it publishes “Statistiques des Systèmes de Paiement” under its statistics section, implying some public reporting on payment systems ([BEAC – Accueil](https://www.beac.int/)). I did not find a consistent monthly/quarterly dashboard specific to Equatorial Guinea; evidence supports at least ad hoc/periodic reporting at regional level.

revision_notes: Changed from Ad Hoc to Annual. BEAC's Annual Report (Rapport Annuel BEAC 2024) includes a dedicated payment-systems section with detailed tables (SYGMA/SYSTAC operations, incident counts), and BEAC separately publishes a 'Rapport sur les services de paiement dans la CEMAC' (2024 edition) with transaction volumes and values across the CEMAC zone. Together these show a recurring, structured annual disclosure covering the regional systems (SYGMA, SYSTAC, GIMACPAY) that Equatorial Guinea participates in, going beyond ad hoc releases, though reporting is CEMAC-wide rather than GNQ-specific. Value Code revised from 2 (Ad Hoc) to 3 (Annual).

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: World Bank states Equatorial Guinea has no national financial inclusion strategy (unique in CEMAC) and that political prioritization of financial inclusion could be reinforced; it mentions regional financial inclusion strategy design but no clear domestic pro-poor governance/representation mechanisms tied to payments ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). Evidence of a humanitarian cash transfer pilot after the 2021 Bata explosion suggests some inclusion-oriented programming but not a governance mechanism ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial. The CEMAC Regional Financial Inclusion Strategy (SRIF, 2025-2029) explicitly targets vulnerable groups (women, youth, rural populations, and refugees/migrants as a secondary target), aiming to raise financial inclusion from 32% (2021) to 60% by 2029, showing an emerging pro-poor orientation at regional level. AfricaNenda's SIIPS assessment of GIMACPAY notes governance is 'progressed' but could still add stronger consumer recourse mechanisms. No Equatorial Guinea-specific governance mechanism (e.g. dedicated consumer board seats) was found. Value Code 2 (Partial) confirmed.
